submission.natural_language_explanation:
This last-layer head attends one-hot to a single already-read delimiter token - the most recent line-break token, or, before any line break, the text's first token or an earlier ';'/',' - and copies that token's value into the residual, so at the end of a line it raises the next-token logits of carriage-return line breaks ('', '
') and strongly lowers bare '
', i.e. it sustains the document's own CR/indentation line-ending convention. Strength is the copied value's distance from the head's mean write, so it reaches 2.4-2.9 where the copied token carries a carriage return or two or more tabs (e.g. '
		', '
		'), 1.0-2.0 for a plain '
', '
	' or a copied ';'/',' ~0.25-0.35 when only the text's first token is available (single-line prose), and the one other large target is a rare word-initial capital token (proper-noun start, 1.6-2.4).
